To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a T-cell line generated from murine TILs can be established that can mediate in vitro and in vitro antitumor effects and that combinations of lymphohokines, which alone do not affect tumor burdens, can synergize with T-cell-mediated immunotherapy.
the antitumor activity of a T-cell line derived from murine TILs can be augmented in vitro by cytokine pretreatment of the tumor and in vivo by combination cytokine treatment with TILs.
a murine TIL clone can be maintained and used to study in vitro and in vitro antitumor mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of tumor-specific TILs, the effect of cytokine pretreatment of tumors on TIL antitumor activity, and the effect of combinations of TILs and lymphokines on tumor burdens in vivo.
understanding and developing immunotherapies for cancer.
the generation of tumor-specific T-cell clones from murine tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TIIs) and the study of their antitumor effecacy in vitro and in in vivo tumor models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TIL line BF-1 is an excellent model for the study of the antitumor effects of TILs.
the TILs, which are the cells of interest for the treatment of cancer, are capable of killing tumor cells and that this killing is increased when the tumor is treated with IFN-gamma and TNF.
the combination of cytokines, which when given alone do not affect tumor growth, can synergize with adoptively transferred lymphokine-primed lymphocytes to mediate antitumor effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cytokines can be used to increase the susceptibility of tumor targets to lysis by TILs and that combinations of cytokines and TILs can be used in the treatment of metastatic disease in mice.

we have demonstrated that TILs can be expanded in vitro, that this expansion can be maintained for long periods of time, that the TILs generated in vitro are specific for the tumor from which they are derived, and that they can be used for the treatment of established metastatic tumors.
TILs, in combination with IL-2, are capable of mediating antitumor effects in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TILs can be established from murine tumors and used to mediate antitumor effects in vitro and in the treatment of micrometastases.
cytokines may have a synergistic effect on the antitumor effects of TILs, and thus may be useful in the treatment of human cancer.
the combination of TILs and cytokines is a powerful tool in cancer therapy.
